sentences.text: 4. Petitioner is represented by his father, General Power of Attorney Holder.
Copy of the GPA is enclosed along with the application.
5. Respondent No.2 is present before the Court and identified by her counsel.

She has filed an affidavit, wherein, she has sought permission to compound the offence and expressed for closure of the proceedings now pending before the trial Court, in view of the amicable settlement.

Paragraph Nos.1 to 11 of the affidavit are extracted here under:-
I, Husnara Kamal Shaik, W/o Arif Ahmed, aged about 33 years, residing at No. 27, 1st Floor, 5th Cross, NC: 2025:KHC:50336 HC-KAR 1st Main, Ilyas Nagar, J.P. Nagar,
Bangalore- 560078, do hereby solemnly affirm and state as under:
1.
That I am the Respondent No.2 in the said criminal petition and are conversant with the facts of the case and thereby competent to swear this affidavit.
2. I state that the Petitioner is my husband/Accused in the case and I am the de facto complainant.

3. I state that my marriage with the Petitioner was solemnized on 13.12.2014 at Suryodaya Convention Hall, B-39/2, Bannerghatta Road, Behind Sagar Automobiles,
Near Dairy Circle, Bengaluru 560029, in accordance with Muslim rites, customs and traditions, in the presence of their family members, relatives and well-wishers and the marriage was duly registered on 17.01.2015 before the Wakf Officer, District Wakf Office, Karnataka State Board of Wakfs, Bengaluru 560002, vide Marriage Certificate No. DWAC/06/MC/BNU/2014-2015.
4.

I state that I filed a private complaint bearing PCR No 3668/2021 before the learned XXXVII ACJM, Bengaluru against the Petitioner, on the same as per the order the Respondent No. 1 the Basavanagudi Women's PS Bengaluru has registered an FIR bearing No 70/2021.

I further state that the Respondent No.1 police acting upon the FIR has filed a chargesheet before the learned XXXVII ACJM, Bengaluru against the Petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A) and 506 of NC: 2025:KHC:50336 HC-KAR the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P Act, 1961 and the same is registered as C.C. No. 29448/2021.
5.

I state that I have filed a suit bearing O.S. No. 515/2025 before the Learned VI Addl. Principal Family Judge, Bengaluru seeking for dissolution of my marriage with the Petitioner under Sections 2(ii), 2(iv) and 2(viii)(a) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 read with Order VII Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

entities.text: VI Addl. Principal Family Judge, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. I state that upon the matter being referred to the Bangalore, Karnataka Mediation Centre, we have settled our marital disputes amicably.

sentences.text: 7. I state that, upon the intervention of the mediator and well-wishers, I have reached an amicable settlement with the petitioner with regard to our marital disputes.
8. I state that the petitioner and I have mutually agreed to dissolve our marriage.
I further state that the petitioner has agreed to return my jewelry and to pay me Rs. 68,00,000/- (Rupees Sixty-Eight Lakhs only).

9. I further state that I have agreed to the closure/withdrawal of the proceedings in C.C. No.
29448/2021 pending before the Learned XXXVII ACJM, Bengaluru, as I have settled my disputes with the Petitioner.
I further state that there is no objection for allowing the accompanying application as the disputes have been amicably settled as explicitly mentioned above 11.

I state that the said criminal proceedings arose due to a marital dispute between me and the Petitioner and is not a heinous offence against the State and I further state that the same may be compounded.

6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Jitendra Raghuvanshi and others v. Babita Raghuvanshi and another reported in 2013(2) Crimes 90(SC), has held that 'the inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., are wide and unfettered.

entities.text: Jitendra Raghuvanshi and others v. Babita Raghuvanshi and another reported in 2013(2) Crimes 90(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the duty of the Courts to encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes, particularly, when the same are on considerable increase.

Even if the offences are non-compoundable, if they relate to matrimonial disputes and the Court is satisfied that, the parties have settled the same amicably and without any pressure, for the purpose of securing the ends of justice, NC: 2025:KHC:50336 HC-KAR Section 320 of the Code, would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing of FIR.
7. Matter arises out of matrimonial dispute and respondent No.2 has expressed her desire to close the proceedings initiated by her in terms of the settlement.
In view of the settlement between the parties, no purpose will be served by continuing the criminal proceedings against the petitioner.
Hence, it is expedient to quash the proceedings, in the interest of justice.

Accordingly, the following:-
ORDER i) Application is allowed, consequently, petition is allowed.

ii) Entire proceedings in C.C.No.29448/2021 pending on the file of XXXVII ACJM,
Bengaluru are quashed.

iii) In view of the quashing of proceedings against the petitioner, if there is any lookout notice issued in this NC: 2025:KHC:50336 HC-KAR case, the same shall be Mr Arif Ahmed vs State Of Karnataka on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142437913/
4 withdrawn by the concerned police.
I.A.No.1/2024 and I.A.No.1/2025 are disposed of.
